A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PEARL research. Their main text, appendices, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated or renumbered in v4.

before.justification: v3 reports original PEARL experiments on CIFAR-100, TinyImageNet and ImageNet-R, including accuracy measurements, ablations, forgetting analyses and inference timings.

after.justification: v4 retains original PEARL experimental results in the main text and appendices, including benchmark performance, ablations and resource-allocation analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same task-vector construction, SVD-based rank allocation, threshold clipping, weight reinitialization, training and inference procedures. Adding E1/E2 epoch labels to Section 3.3 clarifies the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same CIFAR-100, TinyImageNet and ImageNet-R coverage, Class-IL and Task-IL scenarios, and ImageNet-1K/21K pretraining sources. The pretraining and class-order experiments moved into the main text already appeared in v3.

E2.justification: v4 Table 13 removes CLS-ER, IMEX-Reg and SARL from the corresponding CNN benchmark comparison in v3 Table 10. Other comparator sets are retained. The orthogonal-subspace methods introduced in Appendix B.5 receive conceptual discussion only.

E3.justification: The task splits, image sizes, metrics, backbones, replay-buffer settings, training budgets and evaluation procedures remain unchanged. The relocated fixed-rank, pretraining and randomized-class-order experiments retain their original settings.

E4.justification: The rank, target-module, reinitialization, pretraining, class-order, forgetting and resource-allocation analyses are retained. Several move into Section 4. The new sensitivity discussion adds no experiment and refers to the existing Figure 5.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same three-run averaging and standard-deviation reporting, five randomized class orders, and three-run resource-allocation visualization. No new uncertainty-estimation procedure or significance test is reported.

E6.justification: The twelve accuracy entries for CLS-ER, IMEX-Reg and SARL in v3 Table 10 disappear from v4 Table 13. These include SARL's TinyImageNet Task-IL result of 71.56±0.18%. All retained table values and plotted results are unchanged after matching relocated material.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1, Equations 1–5, and the FFM/CFM definitions in Equations A58–A59 retain the same mathematical content. No proof, derivation or formal assumption is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about rehearsal-free continual learning, dynamic task-specific and layer-specific rank allocation, applicability across three architectures, and outperforming the considered baselines.

C2.justification: Appendix A adds a limitation concerning the choice of task-proximity criterion. New Appendix B.4 explains that poorly conditioned task vectors and SVD noise can cause rank over-allocation or under-allocation. Its discussion of semantic similarity and seed-dependent allocation largely repeats v3 Appendix B.15.

D1.justification: v3 Appendix C is retained as v4 Appendix D, with the same backbone implementation, optimizer settings, batch sizes, learning rates, epoch budgets and LoRA scaling information. No code/data access or other reproducibility information changes.

R1.justification: New Appendix B.5 positions PEARL against orthogonal-subspace methods, citing Chaudhry et al. (2020) and Wang et al. (2023c). Five previously cited works disappear, including the sources for CLS-ER, IMEX-Reg and SARL. Most research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Five existing appendix analyses move into Results as Sections 4.3, 4.4 and 4.7–4.9, and Results is reorganized into nine numbered subsections. Limitations becomes a standalone Appendix A, with the remaining appendices reorganized. This substantially changes document structure despite mostly retained prose.

P2.justification: v4 substantially changes typography, margins, headers, the title/author block and table layout. Four appendix tables and the parameter-isolation comparison figure move into the main text, with widespread resizing and reflow. Plot contents remain unchanged; the CNN benchmark table loses three rows.

improvement.justification: v4 improves organization and adds useful sensitivity caveats, but removes three informative baseline comparisons without replacement or explanation. In v3 Table 10, SARL's TinyImageNet Task-IL mean of 71.56% slightly exceeds PEARL's 71.49% and 70.94%; v4 Table 13 omits this competitive result while retaining broad superiority language. The loss of comparative evidence outweighs the limited explanatory gains.
